lawyer:
Abdul Malek, Senior Advocate instructed by Shamsul Haque Siddique, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants. 
M Shamsul Alam, Deputy Attorney-General, instructed by Zinnur Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Nowabul Alam and others ------ Appellants.
Vs. 
State ----- Respondent.
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: 36 accused persons, including the four accused-appellants before us, stood their trial before the learned Sessions Judge, Narail in Sessions Case No. 22 of 1986 variously under sections 148/307/302/34 of the Penal Code for the murder of Ekhlasuddin Ahmed and his son Ehsanul Huq @ Tunu and for attempted murder of Ekhlasuddin's nephew PW 2 BM Sukur Ali @ Pilu and by judgment and order dated 22.3.88 the learned Sessions Judge, Narail convicted 10 accused persons, including the four accused-appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to death and acquitted the remaining 26 accused persons of the charges against them. The resultant Death Reference No. 28 of 1990 (Dhaka)/2/82 (Jessore) was rejected by the High Court Division, maintaining the order of conviction passed against the four appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, but commuting the sentence of death to imprisonment for life. The appeals preferred by these appellants were dismissed, but the appeals of the other six condemned prisoners were allowed and they were acquitted of the charges. 

 4. PW 2 BM Sukur All @ Pilu, PW 3 Amirul Haque @ Dulu, PW 4 Abdul Wahab and PW 5 BM Imdadul Huq (Tulu), of whom PWs. 2, 3 and 5 are full brothers and are nephews of deceased Ekhlasuddin, are the eye-witnesses to the occurrence and the prosecution case which transpired from their common evidence is, that deceased Ekhlasuddin Ahmed and his son deceased Ehsanul Huq @ Tunu and Ekhlasuddin's nephew PW 2 BM Sukur Ali @ Pilu started on a motor-cycle for Jessore from their village home at Bendarchar, Police Station Kalia, District Narail on 11.6.85 at about 6-45 AM. Deceased Ekhlasuddin had some business at Jessore with his Advocate Nurul Islam and had to cross the river Nabaganga miles away from his house by boat at a place called Baraipara Kheyaghat. Ekhlasuddin asked his nephew PW 5 BM Imdadul Huq @ Tulu to go to Baraipara Kheyaghat to escort him. Accordingly PW 5 took PW 3 Amirul Huq @ Dulu, his brother, with him. They started on foot towards the ghat situated about 1-1/2 miles on the north-west from their house at 6-00 AM. On the way PWs 3 and 5 found PW 4 Abdul Wahab who also accompanied them with the purpose of escorting deceased Ekhlasuddin and his two companions. On the way deceased Ekhlasuddin and his two companions met PW 1 Ekramul Huq (Tuku), who is also Ekhlasuddin's nephew. PW 1 was the sitting Chairman of Kalia Pourashava when he was deposing. Ekhlasuddin and his two companions also stopped at the house of PW 11, Kamalakshmi, a Commissioner of Kalia Pourashava under PW 1 when he was deposing and told him that Ekhlasuddin would go to Narail the next day at about 6-55 AM. PWs 3, 4 and 5 walking on foot came up to the end of the Kalia Pourashava boundary, about 200/250 yards away from the Kheyaghat on the bank of the river Nabaganga, where a dilapidated signboard of the Pourashava was hanging. That was about 7-00 AM. Deceased Ekhlasuddin and his two companions crossed PWs 3, 4 and 5 at the spot where the signboard was hanging and when they reached the bank of the river PWs 3, 4 and 5 saw from a distance of 200/250 yards that the accused persons hiding themselves in the adjoining Kashban from before came out of it variously armed with deadly weapons like gun, ramdao, gupti, dagger, etc. Appellant Nawabul Alam was holding a gun. Appellant Khalilur Rahman passed an order to finish the three of them. Nawab opened fire on the chest of Ekhlasuddin's son Tunu and appellant Idris and 8/9 other acquitted accused persons assaulted Tunu by ramdao. Acquitted accused Latifur gave a gupti blow in his belly and Tunu died. Appellant Khalilur Rahman gave a ramdao blow on the head of deceased Ekhlasuddin which he resisted by his right hand resulting in the severance of his thumbs. Appellant Kawsar Munshi gave a ramdao blow on the head of Ekhlasuddin on the impact of which his brain substance came out. Other acquitted accused persons also gave ramdao blows on the body of Ekhlasuddin who died on the spot. Acquitted accused Jadan and Johur caught hold of PW 2 Pilu and acquitted accused Quddus gave a ramdao blow on his back resulting in injury. Other acquitted accused persons dropped the dead body of Ekhlasuddin in the river. Acquitted accused Hobi and Lutfur arc full maternal uncles of PW 2 Pilu. They ordered Jadan, Johur and Quddus not to kill him and so they left PW 2 who jumped in the river. The accused persons then went away. PWs 3, 4 and 5 who were watching the occurrence from 200/250 yards away taking shelter inside the kashban came up to the bank of the river after the departure of the accused persons and collected the dead body of Ekhlasuddin. PW 1 Ekramul Huq @ Tuku, PW 6 Abdul Malek Sheikh, PW 7 Sobhan, PW 11 Kamalakshmi and others came to the place of occurrence and PWs 2-5 told them the story of the case. PW 1 and PWs 6-8 and 10-11 saw some of the accused persons running away with deadly weapons in their hands immediately after the occurrence. 

 5. Police Station Kalia lies 2 miles to the cast of place of occurrence. PW 14 Sub-Inspector Sk. Wahidur Rahman was the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station on the day of occurrence in the absence of the regular Officer-in-Charge. He stated in his evidence that on 11.6.85 PW 10 Alamgir, PW 4 Abdul Wahab and Laik (not examined) informed him at the Police Station that Ekhlasuddin and his son were killed by some miscreants at Baraipara Kheyaghat. He informed the Superintendent of Police of Narail District over wireless, made a General Diary Entry at 7-20 AM noting the informants names and substance of the information and went to the place of occurrence and found the two dead bodies. He prepared the inquest reports at the Police Station making reference to the General Diary Entry. The Deputy Commissioner, Super-intendent of Police and Officer-in-Charge of Narail came to the place of occurrence at 10-00 AM and asked about the occurrence. At 11-15 AM he sent the dead bodies to the morgue through Assistant Sub-Inspector Abdul Hai and five police constables. He seized blood-stained earth, cartridge, two pairs of sandals belonging to the two deceased persons, a motorcycle and prepared a seizure list, Ext. 3. On the spot the Officer-in-Charge of Narail Police Station was appointed the 10 of the case as also the Officer-in-Charge of Kalia Police Station. PW 16 Abdul Mannar on being so appointed went to Police Station Kalia at about 12 noon when PW 1 Ekramul Huq (Tuku) accompanied by PW 2 Pilu and PW 5 Tulu lodged an FIR (marked Ext. 4(1) with objection) with him at 12-30 PM which he recorded on the dictation of PW 1. He came back to the Police Station immediately thereafter, prepared a sketch map and index and examined some witnesses in the course of the next 3 days when on 14.6.85 PW 17 ABM Abu Taleb Mollah of the Criminal Investigation Department assumed the charge of the investigation of the case on behalf of the Criminal Investigation Department. Upon examination of some more witnesses and completion of investigation he submitted charge-sheet against the accused persons. 

 6. The defence does not deny the factum and place of occurrence but challenges the manner of it and the time. The defence case is that deceased Ekhlasuddin was an MP from Awami League between 1973-75. He was a Member of the Central Committee of BAKSAL when Awami League was split up. During his tenure as MP Rakshi Bahini was stationed at Narail and deceased Ekhlasuddin guided them. Rakshi Bahini had perpetrated atrocities upon the local people for which Ekhlasuddin had earned many enemies. The informant party and the accused persons are bitterly and inimically disposed towards each other. Golam Hossain and Maya, father and maternal uncle respectively of appellant Nawabul Alam were murdered in 1984. Deceased Ekhlasuddin, PW 1, PW 3, PW 4, PW 5 and PW 11 amongst others were accused in the said murder case the sessions trial (Sessions Case No. 65 of 1985) of which was pending at the time of occurrence. Ekhlas Uddin and his son were murdered at the Kheyaghat not at 7-00 AM as alleged by the prosecution but at 5-45 AM by some unknown miscreants. He, his son and nephew Pilu did not come to the Kheyaghat from his village home as alleged but from an unknown place and PWs 3, 4 and 5 did not come to the Pourashava boundary to see him off. They were not present at the place of occurrence at the time of occurrence and they did not see the occurrence at all. PW 2 jumped into the river at the time of assault by unknown miscreants and did not see the happenings at all. Two boatmen residing in the bank of the river, Bachon Majhi and Shona Majhi who used to run boats in the Nabaganga river saw the dead bodies and informed the relations of deceased Ekhalasuddin at Bendarchar 1-1/2 miles to the south-east. On receiving the information PW 10 Alamgir, PW 4 Abdul Wahab and Laik (not examined) went to Police Station Kalia at 7-20 AM and upon the information obtained from them PW 14 made a General Diary Entry which spoke of "some miscreants" being responsible for the murders. The accused persons were not named in the General Diary Entry nor was it mentioned that anybody had seen the miscreants. PW 14 started an investigation on the basis of the General Diary Entry. The names of the accused persons were not disclosed to anyone of the hundreds of people who arrived at the place of occurrence after the dead bodies were recovered, including high officials. The accused persons being enemies were roped in as an afterthought. 

 7. Appellant Nawabul Alam is he head of his family. Appellant Khalilur Rahman was elected Chairman of the Local Union Council defeating PW 1 Ekramul Huq and an election case against both appellants Nawabul Alam and Khalilur Rahman instituted by PW I was pending at the time of occurrence. Appellant Kawser Munshi is the father-in-law of appellant Nawabul Alam. Kawser Munshi's elder brother acquitted accused Lal Miah was at the material time the Chairman of Kalia Union Parishad. The other accused persons are close relations and party men to appellant Nawabul Alam who had political and family rivalry and enmity with deceased Ekhlasuddin and his nephew PW 1 Ekramul Huq for many years last past. The informant party led by PW 1 Ekramul Huq in consultation with Awami League leaders who arrived at the scene concocted this false story against the accused persons. Some of the accused persons also pleaded alibi. 

 9. The trial Court (as also the High Court Division) rejected Ext. 4(1) as an FIR of the case and treated the same to be a statement of PW 1 under section 161 CrPC. The General Diary Entry (proved by the defence Ext. A) was treated to be the FIR being earliest in point of time and being also the basis of investigation started by PW 14. The trial Court found no inconsistency regarding the occurrence in the evidence of the eye-witnesses. The prosecution led evidence that PW 4 Abdul Wahab did not accompany PW 10 Alamgir and Laik to the Police Station and that it was Wahab's full brother Nawab who accompanied PW 10 and Laik to the Police Station. Nawab, Wahab and Laik are full brothers and residents of Bendarchar. The trial Court was not clear as to how Wahab's name was entered in the General Diary Entry, but it accepted the suggestion strangely coming from the prosecution that PW 14 Sub-Inspector Wahidur Rahman had enmity with deceased Ekhlasuddin and therefore he may have reason to damage the prosecution case for which the investigation of the case was made over to the officer-in-charge of Narail Police Station. No clear finding was given by the trial Court as to whether Nawab or Wahab went to the Police Station. As the ballistic expert PW 18 Fazlur Rahman was not sure as to from which gun, that of appellant Nawabul Alam and acquitted accused Lal Miah, deceased Tuku was fired upon, the trial Court did not find corroboration of the prosecution case from the evidence of PW 18. As for PWs 6 and 7 the trial Court clearly held that their recognition of the accused persons from 250/300 yards away in the middle of the river was not free from doubt. The trial Court, therefore, discarded their evidence. It clearly held that there was controversy with regard to PW 4 Wahab being an eye-witness but as PW 2 Pilu, an injured witness in the same occurrence, has been corroborated by PWs 3 and 5 they cannot be disbelieved for being interested witnesses. Then the learned Sessions Judge observed as follows: 

 10. In its search for a neutral witness as corroborative of the evidence of PWs 2, 3 and 5, the trial Court found support from the evidence of PW 8 Shamsur Rahman and found no reason to disbelieve him. PW 8 stated in his evidence that in the morning of 11.6.85 he heard a gunshot and found 10 accused persons running away with weapons in their hands. It is those 10 persons including the four appellants whom the learned Sessions Judge convicted under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced to death. Of them accused Dhalu Kha, Into Kha and Quddus were not even charged under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, but the learned Sessions Judge altered the charge to one under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code after conclusion of evidence and in their absence and found them guilty of the charge. The plea of alibi of some of the accused persons was rejected on consideration of the evidence of DWs. 

 15. It has been accepted by both the trial Court and the High Court Division that the PWs whose evidence have been relied upon arc closely related to deceased Ekhlasuddin and are partisan and interested witnesses. PWs 2, 3 and 5, who are tie eye-witnesses are full brothers and they are the sons of deceased Ekhlasuddin's full brother. PW 1 is also a nephew of Ekhlasuddin and PWs 1, 2, 3 and 5 live in joint houses along with deceased Ekhlasuddin at Bendarchar. Deceased Ekhlasuddin and PWs 1, 2, 4, 5 and 11 amongst others are co-accused in Golam Hossain and Belayet murder case which was started in 1984. PW 4 Wahab and his brother Nawab and Laik live 300 cubits to the west of the house of PWs 2, 3, and 5. Mr. Shamsul Alam, learned Deputy Attorney-General, also frankly concedes that these witnesses are close relations of deceased Ekhlasuddin and they had long-standing enmity with the accused appellants. 

 17. The principle that is to be followed is that the evidence of persons falling in the category of interested, interrelated and partisan witnesses must be close and critically scrutinised. They should not be accepted on their face value. Their evidence cannot be rejected outright simply because they are interested witnesses for that will result in a failure of justice, but their evidence is liable to be scrutinised with more care and caution than is necessary in the case of disinterested and unrelated witnesses. An interested witness is one who has a motive for falsely implicating an accused person and that is the reason why his evidence is initially suspect. His evidence has to cross the hurdle of critical appreciation. As his evidence cannot be thrown out mechanically because of his interestedness, so his evidence cannot be accepted mechanically without a critical examination. As Hamoodur Rahman, J. (as his Lordship then was) observed in the case of Ali Ahmed Vs. State 14 DLR (SC) 81: 

 18. It is also instructive to note the following observations of the Indian Supreme Court in the case of Masalti Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, 1965 AIR (SC) 202: 

 19. The rule that the evidence of interested witnesses requires corroboration is not an inflexible one. It is a rule of caution rather that an ordinary rule of appreciation of evidence. The Supreme Court of Pakistan spelt out the rule in the case of Nazir Vs. State, 14 DLR (SC) 159 as follows: 

 ".....we had no intention of laying down an inflexible rule that the statement of an interested witness (by which expression is meant a witness who has a motive for falsely implicating an accused person) can never be accepted without corroboration. There may be an interested witness whom the Court regards as incapable of falsely implicating an innocent person. But he will be an exceptional witness and, so far as an ordinary interested witness is concerned, it cannot be said that it is safe to rely upon his testimony in respect of every person against whom he deposes. In order, therefore, to be satisfied that no innocent persons are being implicated along with the guilty the Court will in the case of an ordinary interested witness look for some circumstances that gives sufficient support to his statement so as to create that degree of probability which can be made the basis of conviction. That is what is meant by saying that the statement of an interested witness ordinarily needs corroboration." 

 21. As already stated at 7-20 AM on the fateful day of murder PW 10 Alamgir, PW 4 Wahab and Laik informed the Police Station about the murder without disclosing the names of the accused persons, on the basis of which PW 14 made a General Diary Entry, Ext. A. PW 4 Wahab later turned out to be an eye-witness to the occurrence and he as well as PWs 1 2, 3 and 5 all in one voice denied of having known anything about the General Diary Entry except when they were deposing. PW 4 deposed that he did not go to the Police Station at all, His brother Nawab went there. PW 10 Alamgir also deposed that Nawab and Laik were with him when he went to the Police Station. PW 4 Wahab was not with him. PW 14 Sk Wahidur Rahman clearly stated in his evidence that PW 10 Alamgir, PW 4 Wahab and Laik went to the Police Station and informed him about the occurrence. There is absolutely no suggestion to him that he had mistaken Nawab for Wahab or that he interpolated the General Diary Entry in any manner. The prosecution without taking leave from the Court cross-examined PW 14 SI Sk Ohidur Rahman and brought out from him that deceased Ekhlasuddin had filed two cases of looting against him in which charge-sheet was submitted against him. His enmity with deceased Ekhlasuddin is admitted and that may be the reason for his instant removal as 10 of the case but that still does not explain why he will write SM Abdul Wahab and not Nawab Ali as one of the three informants. The prosecution has not examined Laik and Nawab and has not given any explanation for their non-examination. The General Diary Entry Ext. A and the entries therein not only emerge unscathed by the evidence on record but it is also on record that the two inquests on the dead bodies were made by PW 14 in presence of PWs 1 and 2 who signed in the inquest reports which contain a specific reference to the General Diary Entry. PW 1 is a matriculate and PW 2 was a higher secondary student at the material time. The seizure lists Ext. 3 prepared by PW 14 also contain a reference to the General Diary Entry and PWs 4, 5 and 10 are signatories to Ext. 3. PW 4 has passed I Corn Examination, PW 5 is a Law student and PW 10 is a literate person. It is inconceivable that they would put their signatures on the inquest reports and seizure lists without reading the contents thereof, including the General Diary Entry. That PW 4 Wahab did not go to the Police Station and that his brother Nawab went there have not been established beyond reasonable doubt. No conclusion has been drawn by either Court below that the insertion of Wahab in place of Nawab was mistake or on interpolation. There is nothing on record to show nor there is any suggestion that PW 14 failed to take proper steps in investigating the case or did anything to benefit the accused till the time Officer-in-Charge Narail was appointed as TO by the SP. Rather it appears from the evidence that whatever he did was in due performance of duty as the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station. The trial Court clearly held that the evidence of PW 4 Wahab as an eye-witness is controversial. The High Court Division has not dealt with this aspect of the case at all and has uncritically accepted the evidence of PW 4 as an eye-witness without resolving the doubt as to whether he went to the Police Station or to the place of occurrence with PWs 3 and 5. It is the defence case that upon receiving the news of the murder of Ekhlasuddin and his son by some assailants on the bank of the river the informant party comprising of PW 4 and his brother Laik and PW 10 Alamgir went to the Police Station and on their information that some miscreants had killed Ekhlasuddin and his son at Baraipara Kheyaghat a General Diary Entry was made by PW 14. If PW 4 Wahab cannot be excluded from the General Diary Entry firmly and unequivocally then not only the defence case is made probable by the evidence on record itself but the prosecution case also becomes vulnerable in that the evidence of PWs 3, 4 and 5 seeing the occurrence together becomes doubtful. 

 22. Further, Police Station Kalia is 2 miles to the east of place of occurrence and from village Bendarchar the Police Station is 1-1/14 miles to the north-east. The place of occurrence is 1-1/2 miles to the northwest of Bendarchar. Whether it is Nawab or Wahab it is not understood why instead of going to the place of occurrence towards the north-west they went to the opposite direction towards the north east towards the house of PW 10 Alamgir which is to the further east of Police Station. The prosecution has led no evidence as to from where Laik, Nawab and/or Wahab went to the house of PW 10 Alamgir and where they were when they received the news of the murder. These unexplained facts, together with the non-examination of Laik and Nawab and the concerted attempt of the PWs at the trial to feign ignorance about the General Diary Entry cast a serious doubt as to whether PW 4 Wahab at all accompanied PWs 3 and 5 to the Kheyaghat from Bendarchar and as to whether he at all saw the occurrence. This doubt will in turn cast a shadow on the evidence of PWs 3 and 5 who said that they were accompanied by PW 4. The High Court Division has signally failed to consider the implication of the collapse of Ext. 4 (1) as an FIR on the prosecution case. 

 23. With the fall of the evidence of PW 4 as an eye-witness the evidence of the other eye-witnesses becomes even more suspect. It is the defence case that deceased Ekhlasuddin had enemies and that he never used to live in the same place to avoid being targeted by his enemies. This case finds support from the cross-examination of PW 4 Wahab who admits that deceased Ekhlasuddin used to stay at Dhaka, Narail, Kumri, Jessore and Kalia. It is also the defence case that on the previous 10th night, deceased Ekhlasuddin was hiding. So whether on the fateful day he really started from his house on a motorcycle at 6-45 AM or not should have been the subject matter of a close scrutiny. None of the Courts below has done that. 

 24. The High Court Division consulted the Muhammadi Pocket Panjika of the relevant year and found that the sun was already tip on the 11th June, 1985 at 5-45 AM. So when Ekhlasuddin started for the Kheyaghat with his deceased son and PW 2 Pilu at 6-45 AM from Bendarhar it was already broad daylight. Yet the only evidence of his journey from his own house comes only from the interested witnesses, namely, PWs 1-5 and 11 and from nobody else. The inmates of the house of the deceased, though examined by the Criminal Investigation Department, have not been examined and no passerby has been produced to establish the origin of Ekhlasuddin's journey. PW 1 Ekramul Huq Qa Tuku stated in his evidence that Ekhlasuddin along with his son and PW 2 proceeded in the motorcycle "from our house" and were going to Jessore to meet Advocate Nurul Islam. PW 2 says otherwise. He says that at about 6-45 AM he, Ekhlasuddin and Tunu started from house by motorcycle for Jessore and they 'met Chairman Tuku who is PW 1". These two versions are entirely different. PWs 3, 4 and 5 do not say anything regard-ing Ekhlasuddin's meeting with anyone on the way. PW 11 Kamalakshimi stated in his evidence that on 11.6.85 he was sitting on the verandah of his southern homestead. Ekhlasuddin and Tunu came to him and Ekhlasuddin called him and told him that he would go to Narail on the next day at about 6-55 AM. Two things are evident in his evidence. First, he does not corroborate the evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 4 that deceased Ekhlasuddin was going to Jessore. PWs 3 and 5 do not say anything about Ekhlasuddin's going to Jessore. Secondly, he does not corroborate the evidence of PW 2 that he was on the motorcycle with Ekhlasuddin and Tunu. PW 11 does not notice PW 2 at all. Nor does he notice the injury of PW 2 after his arrival at the place of occurrence. PW 2 stated in his evidence that we (meaning all three of them) stopped the motorcycle near the house of Kamalakshmi who was told by his uncle that he might come to Narail on the date of case fixed for tomorrow. PW 11 gives no corroboration of the presence of PW 2 in the company of deceased Ekhlasuddin and his son. PW 11 is a co-accused in the Golam Hossain and Belayet murder case and he is a Commissioner of Kalia Pourashava of which PW 1 Ekramul Huq is the Chairman. Therefore, PW 11 is as much an interested and partisan witness as PWs. 1-5. There is thus no satisfactory and unimpeachable evidence on record that deceased Ekhlasuddin, his son and PW 2 started on a motorcycle from their village home at 6-45 AM and that they were bound for Jessore. The trial Court and the High Court Division completely lost sight of this aspect of the case. 

 25. The other group of witnesses who travelled from Bendarchar to Kheyaghat on foot, namely, PWs 3, 4 and 5 also undertook the journey when the sun was up and it is absolutely improbable that they went unnoticed upto the Pourashava boundary, yet there is neither any circumstantial or ocular corroborative evidence in support of their story of journey. Even PW 1 Ekramul Huq does not say anything regarding their journey. PW 5 BM Emdadul Huq @ Tutu stated in his cross-examination, "Tuku (i.e. PW 1) did not know that we went to the ghat for escorting the deceased. I have not told PW 1 that we 3 persons escorted the deceased to the ghat", a strange statement indeed, considering that PW 1 who was engineering the prosecution case and had lodged an abortive FIR ought to have been the first person to know how PWs 3-5 came to be there at the place of occurrence at the time of occurrence. The journey of PWs 3-5 to escort deceased Ekhlasuddin upto the ghat is also doubtful. 

 26. The High Court Division found that all the eye-witnesses described the main occurrence consistently and without any discrepancy and contradiction. That again at times (as, it will be seen, in the present case) is a hallmark of interested testimony and should not be accepted on its face value. PW 2 Pilu was nearest to the occurrence and his version of the events will be more detailed as he had the occasion to observe the events at more close quarters, but PWs 3, 4 and 5 were about 200/250 yards away from the place of occurrence and they were hiding themselves in the Kashban for fear of being attacked by the assailants, but the description of occurrence by PWs 3, 4 and 5 is parrot-like, undistinguishable from that of PW 2. They did not miss anything from 200/250 yards away, even though their opportunity to see from a longer distance from hiding in the Kashban and in a state of fright must have been much more less than that of PW 2. Nabaganga river is about 500/600 yards in breadth and PW 6 Abdul Malek and PW 7 Sobhan, two boatmen who are alleged to have seen the occurrence from the middle of the river, about the same distance from where PWs 3-5 had allegedly seen the occurrence, were disbelieved by the trial Court and the High Court Division on the ground that the occurrence cannot be witnessed properly from such a distance. By the same token the parrot-like evidence of PWs 3-5 ought to have been subjected to a critical review, more so when the vision of PWs 3-5 were clouded by the lush growth of Kashful around them where they took refuge. 

 27. The evidence of PWs 3-5 as eye-witnesses ought to have been subjected to further scrutiny in view of their admission that they did not even think of lodging any FIR, far less lodging any. PW 14 came to the place of occurrence soon after the occurrence, held inquests and seized alamats. The Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police and Officer-in-Charge of Narail Police Station came to the place of occurrence at 10-00 AM and they stayed there upto 12 noon. It is stated by PWs 1-5 uniformly that during this long period of nearly 4-1/2 hours no one thought of lodging an FIR and no written complaint was submitted to the Deputy Commissioner or Superintendent of Police. PW 1 stated in his cross-examination that he found 6 witnesses there and they are not accused in the Golam Hossain and Belayet murder case. About 1,000 people assembled there within half an hour, he stated. There is no evidence that the eye-witnesses disclosed the names of the accused persons to any one of the multitude of people including high officials who assembled there. It is only after the departure of the high officials that at 12-30 PM PW 1 accompanied by PWs 2 and 5 lodged the so-called FIR at Kalia Police Station. By this time the injuries on the dead bodies were fully noticed by the PWs and political leaders of the party to which deceased Ekhlasuddin belonged had arrived at the scene. 

 29. PW 1 Ekramul Huq (Tuku) is totally silent in his evidence as to from whom he heard about the occurrence, he admittedly not being an eye-witness. PW 2 Pilu says that PW 9, PW 7, PW 6, Sattar, Samad and thereafter PW 1 came to the place of occurrence and he told them "the story of the assault", but PW 9 has only been tendered, PWs 1, 6 and 7 do not corroborate him and Sattar and Samad have not been examined without any explanation. PW 3 Amirul Huq @ Dulu stated that PW 1, PW 11, PW 7, PW 9 and others came to the place of occurrence and they (meaning PWs 3-5) told them "the story of the case", but PWs 1 and 7 do not corroborate PW 3, PW 9 has only been tendered and PW 11 says that PWs 2-5 told him and others that the "accuseds killed the deceaseds". Needless to say, there is no corroboration at all in the eye of law. PW 4 Abut Wahab stated that PW 7, PW 9, one Samad Majhi, PW 11 and PW 1 came to the place of occurrence and "we told them the story". There is no corroboration of PWs 1 and 7 on this point, PW 9 was only tendered and Samad Majhi was not examined at all. PW 11 Kamalakshmi's corroboration as stated above has no value. PW 5 stated that PWs 7, 9, 6, Samad, Sattar, PW 1, PW 11, Razzaque, Abu Mollah came to the PO and "we told them the story". PWs 1, 6 and 7 did not corroborate PW 5 at all, Samad, Sattar, Razzaque and Abu Mollah have not been examined without any explanation and the nature of corroboration from PW 11 Kamalakshmi is without any value. 

 35. With regard to the ballistic expert PW 18 Fazlur Rahman the High Court Division found that appellant Nawabul Alam may have fired from the gun of acquitted accused Lai Miah who was his father-in-law, having borrowed it from him, but PW 18 was not at all sure from which of the two seized guns the firing was made. In view of the uncertain nature of the testimony of PW 18, which even the trial Court noticed, it was quite wrong on the part of the High Court Division to come to any conclusion basing on his testimony. 

 42. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 11.6.85 at about 6-45 AM deceased Eklasuddin Ahmed with his son, deceased Ahsanul Huq and PW 2 BK Sukur Ali left their house at Bendarchar on a motor cycle for Jessore to meet their Advocate. While going they met PW 1 Ekramul Huq Tuku, the Chairman of Kalia Pourashava and PW 11 Kamalakshmi and at the end of the Pourashava before a small distance off from the place of occurrence, they also met the eye-witnesses of the occurrence namely, PW 3 Aminul Huq Dulu, PW 4 Abul Wahab and PW 5 Emdadul Huq Tutu. As they reached Baraipara Kheyaghat all the accused persons including these 4 appellants came out from their hiding behind nearby Kashban and suddenly encircled the deceased persons and PW 2 Sukur Ali. On the order of appellant No. 2 Khalilur Rahman, appellant No. 1 Nawabul Alam opened fire with his gun hitting Ehsanul Huq Tulu on his chest causing bleeding injury. Accused appellant No. 4 Idris and other accused persons dealt ram dao blow upon the face and various parts of deceased Tulu and he succumbed to his injury on the spot. At that moment appellant No. 2 Khalilur Rahman dealt a ram dao blow on the head of deceased Eklasuddin which he tried to prevent with his right hand with the result that his right thumb was severed. Appellant No. 3 Kauser Munshi dealt a ram dao blow upon the head of deceased Eklasuddin causing bleeding injury and his brain substance came out. The other accused persons also dealt dao blows upon various parts of his body. As a result of these injuries deceased Eklasuddin also died on the spot. Meanwhile, two other accused persons caught hold of PW 2 BM Sukur Ali Pelu and acquitted accused Quddus dealt ram dao blow on his back with intention to kill him and caused him bleeding injury. The accused persons threw the dead bodies of both Eklasuddin and his son Ehsanul HuqTutu in the river. 

 43. Defence case is that deceased Eklasuddin Ahmed was a Member of Parliament from Awami League till 1975 and he had many enemies and he was living in hiding for fear of his enemies and that the defence suggested that he might have been killed by his enemies. Defence further stated that some of the witnesses of the prosecution saw the entire murder case of Golam Hossain and Belayet Hossain, father and maternal uncle respectively of appellant No. 1 Nawabul Alam and out of that grudge and for pending criminal litigation between the parties, the false case has been started against the accused persons. The defence also took a plea of alibi and in support of that plea examined 11 witnesses. 

 "So far as the details of the occurrence and scenario are concerned all the witnesses are at one with one another. But the main ground on which the evidence of these witnesses is assailed, that the witnesses of the occurrence, particularly the witnesses No. 2-5 who saw the occurrence, are close relations and associates of Ekasuddin. PWs 2, 3 and 5 are full brothers. They are the brothers sons of Eklasuddin. PW is also a nephew of Eklasuddin. It is also admitted that these witnesses were accused in the case of murder of Golam Hossain and Belayet Hossain, respectively the father and maternal uncle of accused appellant Nawabul Alam. Therefore, these witnesses are not only related witnesses but also partisan witnesses." 

 "Thus if it is seen that this PW 2 was present at the scene of occurrence and was also injured in course of the occurrence, great reliance must be placed upon the statement that he saw the assailants. From the suggestion to the PWs 1-5 it is clear that the defence has accepted the position that Pilu was upon the same motor cycle with the deceased at the time of occurrence. But he only escaped." 

 48. PW 2 Pelu was going on the motor cycle of his uncle deceased Eklasuddin Ahmed along with this cousin deceased Ehsanul Huq. He testified that on the way they met Chairman PW 1 Tuku and they stopped their motor cycle near the house of PW 11 Kamalakshmi and Kamalakshmi had talk with his uncle. He also stated that at the end of the Pourashava boundary they met PW 3 Dulu, PW 4 Wahab and PW 5 Tutu. He also stated that accused Jodan and Jahur caught hold of him and acquitted accused Quddus gave a ram dao blow in his back and on being requested by accused Hobi and Lutfor who are his full maternal uncle not to kill him he was let off and he jumped in the river and accused went away. Soon after the eye-witnesses came to the place of occurrence and took the dead bodies of the deceased. According to this witness, PW 1 came to the place of occurrence and he told them the story of assault. PW 3 Aminul Huq @ Dulu is another eye-witness of the occurrence who deposed that his brother PW 5 Tutu asked him to see off uncle Eklasuddin and they started for the Bariaparaghat and he asked PW 4 Wahab to accompany them upto Bariaparaghat. In cross-examination this witness stated that they started on foot at 6-00 AM and their uncle went on motor cycle afterwards. This eye-witness also narrated the details of the occurrence and participation of these 4 appellants in inflicting injuries on the deceased persons. PW 4, another eye-witness, also testified that PWs 3 and 5 told him to accompany them for helping deceased Eklasuddin for going to Jessore. As to the participation of these 4 appellants in killing two deceased persons he gave the same version as given by the other two eye-witnesses PW 2 and 3. PW 5 is another nephew of deceased Eklasuddin who accompanied PWs 3 and 4 on foot upto Bariapara Khayaghat for escorting his uncle deceased Eklasuddin upto that point. This witness also stated in cross-examination that PW 1, PW 11 Kamalakshmi, Razzak, Abu Molla came to the place of occurrence and he told them the story. This eye-witness also stated the details of inflicting of the injuries by the 4 appellants. As a matter of fact there is no discrepancy in the evidence of these four eye-witnesses with regard to the inflicting of injuries by the four appellants and the learned Judges found that they successfully stood the test of scrutiny by the cross-examination of the defence. It is in evidence of PWs 3-4 that they started on foot at 6 AM and deceased Eklasuddin, deceased Tunu and PW 2 started on motor cycle at 6-45 AM. The distance from the house of these witnesses upto Baraipara Khayaghat being Ph miles it is quite natural that they could reach the place of occurrence and saw the occurrence at 7-00 AM. It is quite natural and probable to cover that distance on foot by them. 

 50. PW 11 Kamalakshmi stated that on the day of occurrence deceased Eklas and Tunu came to him while going by motor cycle and the place of occurrence is 500/600 yards from his house. He deposed that hearing the sound of gun fire at the ghat side he went towards Khalyaghat and saw accused Khalilur Rahman, Nawabul Alam, Kausar Molla, Idris and others and they went towards the south and he went to the ghat and found the dead bodies of deceased Eklasuddin and Tunu. This witness further stated that Tunu, Dulu, Wahab and Pelu told him that the accused killed the deceased. This witness is the Commissioner of Kalia Pourashava and an accused in Golam Hossain and Belayet Hossain murder case. He denied the defence suggestion that he did not meet the deceased on the date of occurrence; that he did not hear the sound of gunfire and that he did not go to the place of occurrence after 7-00 AM. He also denied the defence suggestion that he did not see the accused persons running away from the place of occurrence. From the evidence of this witness we find that these 4 appellants were found soon after the occurrence going away from the place of occurrence. He further stated that the eye-witnesses told him that the accused killed the deceased. In the facts and circumstances of this particular case, the learned Judges correctly considered the question of corroboration and observed as follows: 

 "Although corroboration from independent witness is not necessary in the facts and circumstances of this case, as an extreme caution we rely upon PW 11 for satisfactory corroboration since the trial Court who had the advantage of holding the trial felt that corroboration was necessary. Though this PW 11 is a co-accused in Golam Hossain, Belayet murder case he is a man of different community and unrelated to the deceased or any of the witnesses. He was mentioned in the FIR as witness of the occurrence. His house is 500/600 yards away from the place of occurrence. So for finding reassurance we have relied upon the evidence of PW 11. He heard a sound of gun fire at the ghat and went towards the Kheyaghat. There he met accused Quddus who had a ram dao in his hand and ran away at his sight. He also saw accused appellant Khalilur Rahman, Nawabul, Kawsar Munshi, Lal Miah, Hobi, Hannan, Delbar, Metu and others going towards the south from the place of occurrence. He also net PW 5 Tulu, PW 3 Dulu, PW 4, Wahab and PW 2 Pilu at the place of occurrence. He heard of the occurrence from PW. 2 He is a responsible man and also a Commissioner of Kalia Pourashava. So he can be safely trusted although he was involved in the Golam Hossain murder case. Out of these persons whom PW 11 saw running away immediately after the occurrence, accused Khalilur Rahman, Nawabul Alam and Kawsar and Idris have been convicted and rest have been acquitted by the learned Sessions Judge." 

 56. It may be mentioned that deceased Eklasuddin, a former Member of the Parliament of Awami League, a former Chairman of Narail Pourashava and a political figure in the locality along with his son Ehsanul Huq were murdered on 11.6.85 at about 7-00 AM and the General Diary Entry was recorded at Kalia Thana being General Diary Serial No. 321 at 07-20 by PW 14 Sub-Inspector of Police Sk. Wahidur Rahman within about twenty minutes of the occurrence. The General Diary Entry reads that Syed Alamgir, son of Syed Ashraf Ali appearing along with SMA Wahab, son of late Somed Sheik and Laik Sheik, son of late Somed Sheik informed that it was heard that some miscreants killed Eklasuddin and his son Ehsanul Huq at Baraipara Kheyaghat and had thrown the dead bodies on the eastern bank of the river. Immediately after recording the General Diary Entry PW 14 went to the place of occurrence and held inquest on the dead bodies of the deceased. He also immediately informed by wireless to the higher authorities about the murder of Eklasuddin. Soon thereafter in the place of occurrence the Deputy Commissioner, Superintendent of Police, UNO and all other high officials along with many people assembled as the incident relates to the killing of an important political figure in that locality. Mr. Malek's contention is that when the name of SM Abdul Wahab (PW 4), son of late Somed Sheik appeared in the General Diary Entry and when actually he was an eye-witness of the occurrence why no names of the assailants were mentioned in the General Diary Entry few minutes after the occurrence and why it was mentioned that these two persons were murdered by some miscreants. It will be proper in this connection to refer to the relevant evidence on record to appreciate the argument of Mr. Abdul Malek. PW 4 Abdul Wahab, Laik Sk. and Nawab are 3 sons of late Somed Sk. Laik Sk was' not an eye-witness of the occurrence but it is found that Wahab was an eye-witness. From the evidence of Wahab it is found that he did not go to the Police Station to lodge the General Diary Entry. But he was present although in the place of occurrence from 7-00 PM to 12 noon and he was a witness of seizure of Alamats by the Police Officer. Further, PW 16 Abdul Mannan, Officer-in-charge of Narail Police Station, deposed that while recording the statement of PW 4 he found from the statement of this witness that he did not go to the Police Station to lodge the General Diary Entry. PW 16 deposed in cross-examination that in the General Diary Entry the names of Alamgir, Wahab and Laik appears. According to this witness, the two brothers, Nawab and Laik were not made charge-sheet witnesses. He further testified that late Somed Sk. had three sons namely PW 4 Abdul Wahab, Laik Sk and Nawab. The prosecution has explained by adducing evidence of PW 4 Wahab himself and the evidence of PW 16 that PW 4 Wahab was not present at the time of recording the General Diary Entry. Apart from this PW 14 who recorded the General Diary Entry admitted in his examination-in-chief that there is no mention in the General Dairy as to who divulged the information of death in the Police Station. This police officer, PW 14 Wahidur Rahman admitted that he was charge-sheeted due to two cases filed by deceased Eklasuddin and one case lodged by PW 11 Kamalakshmi. It is in the evidence of PW 14 SI Wahidur Rahman, himself that Superintendent of Police, Narail took the case soon after the occurrence from him and handed it to the Officer-in-Charge of Narail Police Station. Thus, the fact remains that the case was withdrawn from this Police Officer. There is another aspect that the General Diary was recorded by PW 14 Wahidur Rahman wherein there is no mention as to who particularly informed the police officer that Eklasuddin and his son were killed by miscreants. PW 14 Wahidur Rahman who recorded the General Diary Entry did specifically mention in his evidence that he did not mention in the General Diary from whom he heard that Eklasuddin and his son were murdered. PW 10 Alamgir whose name appears first in the General Diary Entry testified that Nawab, and Laik Sk. informed him about the murder of Ekhlasuddin and he went to Police Station before going to the Kheyaghat. He further testified that Wahab (PW 4) was not with him, Nawab and Laik were with him while going to Police Station to lodge the General Diary Entry. Thus, on a proper evolution of the General Diary Entry itself and the evidence that has come on record touching the General Diary Entry the prosecution has satisfactorily explained that the entry of Wahab's name is nothing but a mistake as PW 4 Wahab, Nawab and Laik are three brothers. Thus, this argument of the learned Advocate on the General Diary Entry is not at all material and further the other two witnesses whose names appear in the General Diary Entry are not eye-witnesses of the occurrence. 

 64. It must be stated that there cannot be any inflexible rule that the statement of an interested witness can never be accepted without corroboration. If in a given case, it is found that the interested and partisan witnesses are probable and natural witnesses of the occurrence and they definitely identified the appellants and were telling the truth, then they can be safely relied upon even without corroboration. In the present case, the learned Sessions Judge believed the four eye-witnesses and the learned Judges of the High Court Division felt it necessary on account of interested and partisan occular evidence to get some independent corroboration before upholding the conviction of the appellants. 

 65. In the case of Niaz Vs. State reported in 1960 PLD (SC) 387, Kaikaus, J has very elaborately spelt out the nature and corroboration which is required in a case of partisan or interested witnesses. In that reported decision it is found that there were 3 eye-witnesses of the occurrence of murder and the learned Sessions Judge believed all the 3(three) eye-witnesses. The learned Judges of the High Court felt that on account of partisan nature of the ocular, evidence it was necessary to consider whether the words of these 3(three) witnesses could be safely accepted against the accused persons in that case. In that reported decision the learned Judges accepted the corroborative evidence of Khairat Mahmud as true without any discussion of the circumstances which would point to the conclusion that the statement was true. The learned Judges just assumed the correctness of the statement and only considered the effect of its acceptance after accepting that the eye-witnesses are truthful witnesses. In that reported decision, the learned Judges of the Supreme Court of Pakistan on consideration of the evidence of the eye-witnesses found that the eye-witnesses were not truthful witnesses and in that view did not accept their testimonies and consequently, the question of corroboration was meaningless. The primary evidence of the eye-witnesses having been disbelieved by the Supreme Court of Pakistan the corroborative evidence was of no importance at all in the facts of that case.  66. In the case of Nazir and others Vs. State reported in 1962 PLD (SC) 269, Kaikaus, J in considering his observation made in that case of Niaz Vs. State observed as follows: 

 "This is what is meant by saying that the statement of an interested witness ordinarily needs corroboration. For corroboration it is not necessary that there should be the word of an independent witness supporting story put forward by an interested witness. Corroboration may be afforded by anything in the circumstances of a case which tends sufficiently to satisfy the mind of the Court that the witness has spoken the truth. What circumstances will be sufficient as corroboration it is not possible to lay down. But, as the question before the Court would be whether some innocent person had not been implicated in addition to those who were guilty the circumstance relied upon must have a bearing on this question. In the case of an interested witness the corroboration need not be of the same probative force as in the case of an accomplice for the two do not stand on the same footing". 

 67. In the case of Karnail Singh and another Vs. State of Punjab reported in 1954 AIR (SC) 2 it was observed as follows: 

 "The corroboration that is required in such cases is not what would be necessary to support the evidence of an approver but what would be sufficient to "lend assurance to the evidence before them, and satisfy them that the particular persons were really concerned in the murder of the deceased. Vide —Lachhman Singh Vs. State 1952 AIR (SC) 167 at P 169(B), Karnail Singh was arrested on the spot with a spear and a bloodstained pyjama and these are pieces of evidence which would support the inference that he was concerned in the crime".

 71. I have already indicated above, that both the trial Court and the learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record did not think it proper to uphold the conviction of rest of the accused persons and ultimately gave benefit of doubt to them. Apart from defect of framing charge against three accused, benefit of doubt was given to the six accused persons as PW 11 Kamalakhsmi did not involve them in his deposition as found to have seen them going away from the place of occurrence soon after the occurrence. PW 11 Kamalakhsmi has involved these 4 appellants as going away from the place of occurrence. So, this additional circumstance was considered by the learned Judges of the High Court Division. The learned Judges were also not unmindful of the fact that for lack of corroboration from unrelated witnesses some of the accused were given benefit of doubt by the trial Judge and the State has not preferred any appeal against their acquittal order.  (c) That according to the prosecution the occurrence took place at 7-00 AM in the month of June, 1985. So it is not at all difficult from such close proximity on the part of these eye-witnesses to recognise the known persons at 7-00 AM particularly, PW 2 was surrounded at the scene of occurrence along with the deceased persons and was injured in the occurrence.
